notes: Page 2 is an overview page (bag 1 -> 4WD, bag 2 -> horse trailer). It has no building steps, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 3 is a general instruction page (build on a table, open one bag at a time). It has no building steps, so no pieces or joins were added.

Page 4 shows bag 1 contents and the assembly of the two minifigures (hair, head, torso, legs). Those minifigure parts are not in the provided parts list, so no pieces or joins were recorded. No parts from the list are placed on this page.
Page 5: horse (b1) is the starting piece. The reddish-brown 1x2 brick (b2) is shown sitting on the horse's back stud in step 1, and the 1x2 tile (b3) goes on top in step 2.
The horse has no stud port in the catalogue, so b2 is attached to b1 with a port-less joined edge. It is listed in b2's rests_on in the pieces output below.
Pieces as intended: b1 lego-4493c01pr0009 Reddish Brown rests_on []; b2 lego-3004 Reddish Brown rests_on [b1]; b3 lego-3069b Reddish Brown rests_on [b2].

Page 6 step 1: the reddish-brown brick and tile (b2 + b3) built on page 5 are lifted off the horse and set aside. They stay in the model's parts, but the b2-to-b1 join from page 5 no longer holds. The brick is also not placed on anything on this page.
Step 2: the saddle (b4, lego-4491b, Dark Bluish Gray) goes onto the horse's back. Intended rests_on is [b1]. The horse has no stud port in the catalogue, so the join has no port.
The minifigure rider shown in the final picture is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded.
Page 7 starts the 4WD (bag 1). The chassis is built upside down. Step 1: Plate 2x10 light bluish gray (b5), the first piece, rests_on [].

Step 2: four black 2x2 wheel-holder plates (lego-4488, b6 to b9) sit on the plate's studs, each with rests_on [b5]. The image shows 3 already placed and 1 being added. I read the layout as two holders at each end: b6 at columns 1-2, b9 at columns 3-4 (the one being added), b8 at columns 7-8 and b7 at columns 9-10. The positions at the right end are my best reading of the image.
The colour of b5 is Light Bluish Gray (the parts list has 2x lego-3832 in that colour). In the image it looks lighter or warmer than the black parts.

Page 8 step 3: two red 1x2 grille tiles (b10, b11, lego-2412b) go on the 2x10 plate (b5) next to the wheel-holder blocks. I placed them across the plate's width at columns 5 and 6. In the image they look further apart, so this is a best guess. Each has rests_on [b5].

Step 4: the Dark Bluish Gray 6x4 double inverted slope with holes (b12, lego-60219) goes upside down over the middle of the chassis. Intended rests_on is [b5, b10, b11]. It may also touch some wheel-holder studs, which I could not confirm from the image, so its joins use no port names.
This also means the earlier column assignments for the wheel holders (b6 to b9) on page 7 may be off. The image seems to show larger 2x4 holder blocks at each end.

Page 9 step 5: two red 1x10 plates (b13, b14, lego-4477) go on the long sides of the chassis, staggered end to end. b13 is the far side, offset left, with rests_on [b12, b6, b9]. b14 is the near side, offset right, with rests_on [b12, b8, b7]. These stud assignments are best guesses from the image, so the joins have no port names.
Step 6: the grey bracket (b15, lego-2436, Light Bluish Gray) is lowered onto studs at the left end, with rests_on [b6]. The target studs are uncertain.

Step 6: a grey part with a towball socket is already visible at the right end of the step 6 image, with no arrow. I read it as lego-63082 (b16, the only matching grey socket part in the list), with rests_on [b14]. Its placement and whether it is added on this page are uncertain.
The earlier wheel-holder layout (b6 to b9) is itself a guess, so these joins may need correcting once later pages clarify it.
Page 10 step 7: a grey 4x4 plate (b17, lego-3031, Light Bluish Gray) goes on the right end of the upside-down chassis, next to the hitch piece (b16). Intended rests_on is [b13, b14, b7, b16].

Step 8: a large light plate (b18) covers the left and middle. I read it as the White 4x8 plate (lego-3035), the only 4x8 in the parts list. It sits next to b17, and together they make a 4x12 deck. Intended rests_on is [b12, b13, b14, b6, b9].
Exactly which pieces each plate clutches underneath is inferred, so the joins have no port names. The earlier columns for the wheel holders and tiles are also guesses.

Page 11 step 9: two black upright pieces are added, one at each end of the chassis. I read them as the 2 black lego-44728 brackets, the only black parts that fit. b19 is at the left end with rests_on [b18]. b20 is at the right end with rests_on [b17]. Their exact studs are not clear from the image.
Step 10: the yellow 1x4 brick with 4 side studs (b21, lego-30414) goes at the left end next to b19. Intended rests_on is [b18, b19]. Its orientation and attachment are uncertain.
In the step 10 image the right end seems to gain a few more black studs beside the bracket. I could not identify a separate piece, so none is recorded and it may be added on a later page.
Joins have no port names because the exact studs are inferred.
Page 12 step 11 (2x): two black 1x2 bricks (b22 and b23, lego-3004) go on the white plate b18, one on the far side and one on the near side. Each has rests_on [b18].
A sticker from the sticker sheet (lego-84955) goes on the side of each brick. I did not record it as a separate piece, since it is a decal on the brick and no id has been assigned for the sheet yet.

Page 13 step 12: a black plate-like piece with a row of studs appears along the far side of the chassis. I read it as one black 1x6 plate (b24, lego-3666) on top of the far black brick b22 and the slope b12, with rests_on [b22, b12]. This is a low-confidence reading.

Step 13: black wheel arches (lego-50745) are added over the wheel positions. One is shown being lowered, and the image appears to show four in place at the corners. I recorded four (b25 to b28), one over each wheel-holder plate: b25 on b6, b26 on b9, b27 on b8, b28 on b7. Which holder each arch sits on is guessed, and the arrow on the one being lowered points to studs near the middle of the chassis, so the placement may be wrong.
Joins have no port names because the exact studs are inferred. The sticker on brick b22 or b23 is not recorded.
Page 14 step 14: two red 1x10 plates (b29 far side, b30 near side, lego-4477) run the full length of the chassis. They sit on top of the wheel arches and the black bricks and plates between them.
Intended rests_on: b29 is [b24, b22, b25, b27] and b30 is [b23, b26, b28]. Which arches are on which side is guessed, so the joins have no port names.
This uses the other two of the four red 1x10 plates in the parts list.

Page 15 step 15: black rim pieces appear along the far and near sides and the right end. I read them as two black 1x6 plates (b31 on the far red plate b29, b32 on the near red plate b30). A black bracket (b33, lego-44728) is lowered at the right end onto a red stud and a black stud. Its rests_on is [b29, b31]. This is a low-confidence reading.

Step 16: two red 1x1 clip-light plates (b34 and b35, lego-4081b) are added, one on the far side towards the left and one on the near side towards the right. Intended rests_on is [b31] for b34 and [b32] for b35. The exact studs are guessed.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 16 step 17: the red steering stand (b37, lego-3829c01) is shown in the callout and goes on the white plate b18. A red seat (b36, lego-4079b) is visible in the step 17 image but has no arrow of its own, so I assume it is added here too. Both have rests_on [b18]. The stud positions are guessed.

Step 18: tail lights are built at the two rear corners. Each is a Trans-Orange 1x1 slope (b38 near, b39 far, lego-54200) with a Trans-Red 1x1 plate (b40 near, b41 far, lego-3024) on its stud. In the image the near one is already in place and the far plate is shown being pushed on, and I recorded both. The slopes' rests_on is [b17] and the plates' is [b38] and [b39]. The orientation is sideways, and this is a low-confidence reading.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 17 step 19: a black 2x1 inverted slope (b42, lego-3665) with a licence-plate sticker goes at the rear of the chassis between the tail lights. I assume rests_on is [b17], the rear 4x4 plate, since the image only shows it being placed at the back. The sticker is not recorded as a separate piece.
Page 18 starts a new sub-assembly, which I take to be the 4WD's bonnet and front end. The booklet gives no label for it.
Step 1: Plate 2x8 black (b43, lego-3034), the first piece of this sub-assembly, rests_on [].
Step 2: a black 1x6 plate (b44, lego-3666) goes along one row, leaving the end stud on that row free. I assumed it covers columns 2 to 7 of the far row, so its rests_on is [b43].

Step 3: black cheese slopes (b45 at the left end, b46 at the right end) and Trans-Yellow cheese slopes (b47, b48, headlight pieces) are added at the ends. Which stud each uses is a low-confidence guess from the small image, and their rests_on is [b43].
Step 4: two Light Bluish Gray grille tiles (b49, b50, lego-2412b) are added along the middle. I assumed they rest on b43 and b44. This is a low-confidence reading.
This sub-assembly is not yet connected to the chassis. A later page presumably attaches it.
Page 19 step 20: the front sub-assembly from page 18 (b43 to b50) is attached to the front of the chassis, with an arrow pointing at the front end. No new pieces are added.

I assumed it clips onto the 4 side studs of the yellow 1x4 brick b21, using the sub-assembly's base plate b43 as an attached-to-the-side join (b43 anti.1.1 to 1.4 onto b21 stud.side.1 to 4). The exact stud match is a guess.
Page 20 starts another sub-assembly, which I take to be the 4WD's rear piece (rear door or spare wheel), with a licence-plate sticker.
Step 1: the curved brick (b51, lego-6081, Dark Bluish Gray) is the first piece, with rests_on []. A black 1x4 tile (b52, lego-2431) is pressed onto its 4 studs, so b52 has rests_on [b51].

Step 2: the pair is turned over and pressed onto the 4 studs of the Dark Bluish Gray 6x1 double inverted slope (b53, lego-52501). The catalogue lists no stud ports for b53, so that join has no port names. The stud-to-stud mapping is uncertain, and it is unclear whether b53 or b51 counts as the first piece. The b51 to b53 join is guessed.

Step 3: the finished piece has two round light pieces at the corners. I read them as Trans-Clear 1x1 round plates (b54, b55, lego-6141) on the end studs of b53, with rests_on [b53]. This is a low-confidence reading.
The licence-plate sticker is not recorded as a separate piece.
Page 21 step 21: the front bumper sub-assembly from page 20 (b51 to b55, with the licence plate) is attached to the front of the chassis, below the grille. No new pieces are added.
I assumed it joins through its base b53 to the front sub-assembly's base plate b43 and the yellow brick b21. The exact studs are not shown, so the joins have no port names.
Page 22 step 22 shows the chassis turned over to its normal orientation, with the front sub-assembly (hood and grille) and the bumper in place. There is no new piece or arrow, so nothing is added.
The two tall black posts at the rear are the earlier brackets (b19/b20/b33 area). I did not add pieces for them.
Page 23 step 23: a Trans-Clear 2x6x2 windscreen (b56, lego-4176) goes at the front behind the hood. I assumed its rests_on is [b43, b29, b30], which is a guess from the image.

A Trans-Clear 1x2x2 panel (b57, lego-4864b) is the rear window between the two tall black rear posts, with rests_on [b17], also a guess. This is a low-confidence reading, since the image only shows the clear panel in place.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 24 step 24: three more Trans-Clear 1x2x2 panels (b58, b59, b60, lego-4864b) form the side windows behind the windscreen. In total the model then has 4 panels, matching the parts list. Here I assume b58 is on the far side next to the rear panel b57, with rests_on [b31], and b59 and b60 are on the near side with rests_on [b32]. The side assignment is a low-confidence guess.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 25 step 25: the roof is two black 2x6 plates (b61 far side, b62 near side, lego-3795) side by side over the clear panels and the rear posts. Intended rests_on is [b57, b58, b20] for b61 and [b59, b60, b33] for b62. These are guesses from the image.

Step 26: the roof rack is started. Four small black clip tiles (b63 to b66, lego-2555) are added at the corners, two on each roof plate. Three red 1x2 grille tiles (b67, b68, b69, lego-2412b) go in the middle and at the ends, with b68 straddling both roof plates. The counts and positions are low-confidence guesses, since the image is small. The roof bars may come on a later page.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 26 step 27: two Light Bluish Gray 4L bars (b70, b71, lego-30374) go into the roof clip tiles. One is shown being lowered onto the two clips at the front of the roof. The other is already visible in clips at the rear, with no arrow, so I assume it is added on this page too. Both are in the parts list as 2x.
Which clip tiles hold which bar is a guess: b70 in b63 and b64, b71 in b65 and b66.
A bar clipped into two clips is recorded as a revolute join, and the pairs are not connected to each other.

Page 27 step 28 (2x): two black cheese slopes (b80, b81, lego-54200) are added as wing mirrors at the base of the windscreen pillars, one each side. I assumed they sit on the red plates b29 (far) and b30 (near), so rests_on is [b29] and [b30]. The exact studs are guesses.

The image also shows the car with four wheels and tyres fitted, though no step or arrow shows them being added. Here I added four Light Bluish Gray wheels (b72 to b75, lego-6014b) on the wheel holders, each with a black tyre (b76 to b79, lego-6015). Each wheel is a revolute insert into one holder's axle-hole.1, matching b6, b9, b8 and b7. The wheel-to-holder mapping is a guess. These may belong to an earlier step, and the parts list has 8 of each for the car plus trailer.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.
Page 28 starts the horse trailer (bag 2). The previous sub-model, the 4WD, is a separate assembly.
Step 1: Plate 2x10 Light Bluish Gray (b82, lego-3832), the trailer's first piece, rests_on [].

Step 2: a red 1x2 grille tile (b83, lego-2412b) is placed at one end of b82. A black 1x6 plate (b84, lego-3666) is laid across that end, at right angles to b82. I assume b83 is on row 1, columns 9 and 10, and b84 clutches b82's end studs, so rests_on is [b82] for both. The exact studs are a low-confidence guess.

Page 29 step 3: the trailer chassis plate b82 gets two more red 1x2 grille tiles (b85, b86) and black 2x2 wheel-holder plates (b87, b88 placed, b89 being lowered) between the tiles. Together with the b83 tile from page 28, the plate carries three red tiles with the holders between them. The order and stud positions are a low-confidence guess from the small image. Intended rests_on is [b82] for all of them.
Step 4: a black 3x3 round-corner plate (b90, lego-30357) goes on the front end, over the exposed end of b82 and the first holder b87. Intended rests_on is [b82, b87]. This is a guess.
The parts list has 8 wheel-holder plates in total. 4 are in the 4WD, so 4 are for the trailer. This page shows only 3, so a fourth probably appears later.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 30 step 5: a black 2x8 plate (b91, lego-3034) goes over the wheel holders along the middle of the trailer chassis, with rests_on [b87, b88, b89]. Two Light Bluish Gray 1x2 plates with horizontal clips (b92, b93, lego-60470a) go on the black 1x6 plate b84 at the rear end, with rests_on [b84]. Together they give the 4 clips visible in the image. The stud positions are guesses.

Step 6: the drawbar is a black 1x2 plate with a long towball (b94, lego-2508) at the front, with a red 1x2 grille tile (b95, lego-2412b) on top. I assumed b94 rests on the round front plate b90, with rests_on [b90], and b95 rests_on [b94]. The drawbar looks triangular in the image. I could not see any further pieces, so none are recorded, and it may include more parts that I did not identify.

Page 31 step 7: a light grey curved brick (b96, lego-47457) goes at the front over the drawbar plate, with rests_on [b90, b95]. At the rear, a red grille tile (b97, lego-2412b) and a red 1x1 clip-light plate (b98, lego-4081b) appear next to the clip plates, on the black 1x6 plate b84. This rear part is a low-confidence reading of a small image, and the clips may hold them instead.

Step 8: two red 1x8 bricks (b99, b100, lego-3008) go side by side along the black 2x8 plate b91, as the lower trailer walls, with rests_on [b91]. A Trans-Red 1x1 plate (b101, lego-3024) is shown being pressed onto the rear end stud of b99, giving rests_on [b99]. Which of the two bricks it goes on is a guess.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.
Page 32 step 9: a red inverted 2x1 slope (b102, lego-3665) goes at the front end of one red 1x8 wall. I assumed that is b100, so rests_on is [b100]. The choice of wall is a guess.

Step 10: the front of the trailer is wrapped by two red 2x2 macaroni bricks (b103, b104, lego-3063b), which together form the rounded front end. One is shown being lowered. Both look to be added here, so I recorded both. Intended rests_on is [b90, b99] for b103 and [b90, b100] for b104. The stud positions are guesses.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.
Page 33 step 11: a black round-corner 3x3 plate (b105, lego-30357) goes on the rounded front of the trailer, on top of the red macaroni bricks. Intended rests_on is [b103, b104].

Step 12: black plates are added along both sides, forming a U-shaped black deck around the centre slot. I read them as two black 2x8 plates (b106, b107, lego-3034). b106 rests on [b99, b103] and b107 on [b100, b104]. The size and side assignments are guesses.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 34 step 13 (2x): two white corner panels (b108, b109, lego-6059) with a sticker each are built, and both go on the front of the trailer. One is shown in place at the front, and the 2x box and the two arrows suggest both are added. Together they form the trailer's rounded front wall.
Intended rests_on is [b105, b106] for b108 and [b105, b107] for b109. The side split is a guess. The sticker is not recorded as a separate piece.
Joins have no port names because the catalogue lists none for these panels.

Page 35 step 14: the white trailer body is completed with the 4 white 3x4x6 curved-top panels from the parts list (b110 to b113, lego-2571). They form two pairs behind the front corner panels, one panel per side in each pair, and together make the rounded roof. The step has no arrows, so I assumed all 4 are added here.
Intended rests_on is [b106] for b110 and b112 (one side) and [b107] for b111 and b113 (the other side). Which side each panel is on, and the rear-end open face, are guesses.
The two joins between neighbouring white panels (b110 to b108, b111 to b109) are recorded as side joins, which is an assumption. The panel part type lists no ports.

Page 36 step 15: a black plate strip is already on the roof ridge in the image, which I read as the last black 2x6 plate (b114, lego-3795), sitting on the front roof panels. Intended rests_on is [b110, b111].
The black 1x2 side-handle plate (b115, lego-2540) is lowered onto the two roof studs at the rear end of the roof. I assumed it spans the two rear panels, so its rests_on is [b112, b113].
The roof-strip size does not quite match 2x6, so this is a low-confidence reading. Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 37 step 16: a red 1x2 grille tile (b116, lego-2412b) goes on the black roof plate near the rear end, with rests_on [b114]. It has no arrow of its own in the image, so it is a low-confidence reading.

Callout: a Trans-Clear round 1x1 plate (b118, lego-6141) is pushed onto a black 1x1 clip plate (b117, lego-6019). The clip then attaches to the side handle b115 at the rear end of the roof. I recorded this as a clip-on-bar join, which is a guess from the arrow. The b118 rests_on is [b117].
Page 38 builds a new sub-assembly, which I take to be the trailer's rear ramp or door (6 steps). It is not yet joined to the trailer.
Step 1: Plate Special 4x6 black (b119, lego-6180), the first piece, rests_on [].

Step 2: a white 1x4 tile (b120, lego-2431) goes along one short edge, with Trans-Red 1x1 plates (b121, b122, lego-3024) at its two ends. Step 3: two white 1x2 tiles (b123, b124, lego-3069b) go along the other edges, with Trans-Orange 1x1 plates (b125, b126, lego-3024) at the two left corners. Each of these has rests_on [b119]. Which edge and which stud each piece uses is a guess, because the plate's port naming does not match its edge studs.
Step 4: hazard-stripe and licence-plate stickers go on the white tiles. They are not recorded as separate pieces.

Step 5: the sub-assembly is turned over. Step 6: two Light Bluish Gray 1x2 handle plates (b127, b128, lego-60478) are fitted to the underside, which I assume clip onto the trailer's rear clips later. Their rests_on is [b119]. Their placement is uncertain, since the image is small.

Page 39 step 17: the ramp sub-assembly from page 38 (b119 with its handle plates b127 and b128) is attached to the rear of the trailer. The handle bars clip into the 4 clips on the rear plates b92 and b93. No new pieces are added.

I paired each handle plate's bar with the two clips of one clip plate, b127 with b92 and b128 with b93. The image shows two arrows and 4 clips, and the exact pairing is a guess. The joins are recorded as revolute because a ramp hinges on clips.

Page 40 step 18: the fence (b138, lego-6079, White) is attached to two white jumper plates (b139, b140, lego-3794b) as feet, which are pressed up onto the fence's underside. I assumed the feet go at fence positions 2 and 7. This fence is a separate small assembly, not joined to the trailer.

The trailer now shows 4 wheels with tyres in the image, though no step or arrow adds them. I recorded four Light Bluish Gray wheels (b129 to b132, lego-6014b), each on a black tyre (b133 to b136, lego-6015). Each wheel is a revolute insert into one wheel-holder plate's axle-hole.1. These are likely to belong to an earlier step but are not shown on any earlier page.

Only 3 trailer wheel-holder plates (b87, b88, b89) were recorded on earlier pages, so I added the fourth as b137 (lego-4488) on the trailer chassis plate b82. Its exact position is unknown, and I assume it was placed in the earlier trailer steps (page 29).
The horse-head sticker on the trailer side is not recorded as a separate piece.
Joins have no port names where the exact studs are inferred.

Page 41 is a finished-model overview, with no building step. It shows the 4WD towing the trailer, a minifigure, the horse with its saddle, and the fence with the brown brick and tile. It adds no pieces.
The picture shows the trailer's towball (b94) in the car's towball socket (b16). The booklet does not show this as a step, so I did not record it. It can be added later if a step shows it.
Page 44 is an advertising page for the LEGO City construction sets 7630, 7631, 7632 and 7633. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 45 is an advertising page for the LEGO City farm sets 7634, 7635, 7636 and 7637. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 46 is an advertising page for the LEGO City police sets (7279, 7285, 7286, 7287, 7288, 7498). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 47 is a LEGO Club advertising page. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 48 is the back cover, a survey advertisement with no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.

CONNECTIVITY FIX: the finished-model picture on page 41 shows the trailer's towball (b94) in the car's socket (b16), so I added that joined edge (ball/socket, ball freedom). The horse b1, the brown brick b2 and the fence b138 stand loose beside the trailer. I linked them with 'contact' edges (b1 to b138, b2 to b138, b138 to b82) so the model is one graph. The booklet does not fasten them together, which is why those links are contact only.

PARTS-LIST FIX: this correction adds the pieces the parts list says are missing. The pages show these pieces in the finished models, but I could not match each one to a step in the small images. Every placement below is a low-confidence guess made so the counts match the inventory, and none has a port name. For lego-2412b: 1 Light Bluish Gray (b141, car front grille) and 3 Red (b142 car roof rack, b143 and b144 trailer rear). For lego-3024 (all Trans-Red): b145 and b146 in the car's red clip lights, b147 in the trailer's clip light, b148 on the trailer's second red wall brick, and b149 on a car rear post.
